candidates.exact_span: Proposed reissuance of the current National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit issued September 30, 2016, with an effective date of November 1, 2016, and an expiration date of October 31, 2021.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of whether this proposed reissuance became effective, whether the prior permit remained administratively continued, or whether another permit governs during Federal FY2025 would change which enforceable limits (A), monitoring obligations (B), and missing-evidence expectations (C) are treated as applicable for the evaluation period.

Identification of the governing permit number determines which permit terms are linked to reported measurements and monitoring evidence; a different permit association would change limit applicability (A), monitoring requirement scope (B), and how missing-evidence cases are tied to permit conditions (C).

Facility identity scopes which discharge points, parameters, and monitoring records are in scope; a different interpretation of the permitted entity or its coverage would change which limit comparisons (A), monitoring obligations (B), and no-result cases (C) are evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: San Juan River – San Juan Basin
candidates.computation_change_reason: Receiving-water designation can govern which water-quality-based numeric limits apply and whether certain monitoring conditions are triggered; alternate interpretations of the receiving water or basin could change applicable discharge limits (A), condition-dependent monitoring requirements (B), and the basis for classifying missing or conditional monitoring evidence (C).
